Repository: re-cinq/HALEngine
Ticket: #144 Deliver a user's conversation list over the WebSocket protocol

You are editing files in a git repository, mid-way through a ticket that
is already defined by RED acceptance tests. You perform exactly ONE
red-green-refactor round and then stop. Not two. Not "while I'm here".

The ticket's branch is checked out with write access at /var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/bbac9678eaf9/workspace/target.
Run every command from inside it (`cd /var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/bbac9678eaf9/workspace/target` first). The ticket
is at `/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/bbac9678eaf9/workspace/ticket.md`: read it before anything else. Pass `repo` (the
owner/name your task names above) on every `lore_*` call: the gateway has
no checkout to detect it from.

START by reading `.lore/dod.md` on this branch. Its "Done when these pass"
list is the bar; its Facets checklist is where the last round got to. It
names the strategy, the
acceptance tests that define done, and the facets expected. It is the
brief; the ticket below is the context.

RUN ONLY THE TEST YOU WRITE THIS ROUND, by its file, from the package
that owns it, with a deadline — for example `cd <package> && timeout 300 npx
vitest run <file>`. Never run the acceptance tests `.lore/dod.md` lists, nor a
directory that holds them: CI is the judge of this branch, runs them on
every push, and tells you where they stand. Read that from
`/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/bbac9678eaf9/workspace/round-brief.md` when it exists, or ask `lore_get_ci_failures`
— not from your memory, and not from what `.lore/dod.md` predicted. Not
the repository's full suite either, not lint, not the typechecker, not
the formatter. The pod's Bash hook refuses an acceptance test by name and
a runner given no test file.

If this pod cannot run your test — the command that runs it (`java`, `mvn`,
`gradle`, `go`, `cargo`, `dotnet`) is not found, or a wrapper such as
`./mvnw` reports no `JAVA_HOME` — do not look for it and do not install
it: no `sudo`, no `apt`, no `find /`, no download. Do the round from the
code, the tests and CI's verdict, commit and push; CI judges the push,
and a red build comes back to the next round as its brief. Say in your
final message that the round ran no tests here.

YOUR ROUND is the `tdd-loop` skill's three phases, in order, no steps
skipped: one failing test for the smallest facet that moves an acceptance
test closer to green, then the least code that passes it, then refactor
with the bar green. Never edit an acceptance test to make it pass — if an
acceptance test is wrong, stop and say so; that is a failed round.

Under `parallel-change`, all of this happens in the NEW module: leave the
old code alone and working until the acceptance tests are green, and make
the caller switch its own round. Under `characterize`, the
characterization tests are part of the green bar you must keep — a
refactor that reddens them is a behaviour change. Under `mechanical`,
there is no red phase at all: perform the exact edits its Facets
record and commit; the EXISTING tests `.lore/dod.md` names are CI's to
run, and its verdict says whether they stayed green. The diff is the
deliverable, and a round that invents a new test for it has left the
strategy.

Never add a test whose assertion subject is the repo's own source text —
readFileSync of a src/ or test file, a regex over another test,
counting a literal across files. That pins prose, not behaviour: where
prose must agree with a value, make the prose compute the value instead.

TRACEABILITY:
- Each test validates a statement in a spec or ADR. Add the inline
  parenthetical on that statement in the repository's established form —
  `Statement. ([validated by name](path/to/test.ts#L42))`. Inserting a
  test shifts every #Lnn link below it: when the repository has
  `scripts/spec-links/reanchor.mjs`, run
  `node scripts/spec-links/reanchor.mjs` from the repository root after
  the formatter — it moves each link to its test's current line, by test
  title, and prints the links it could not map, which you fix by hand.
  Without it, re-verify every existing #Lnn link on the statements you
  touch yourself.
- Stamp the test's spec anchor (the "specs/<path>#<ordinal>" it
  validates) so the repo's tests.list surfaces it as the descriptor's
  `spec` field and the VALIDATED_BY link is established automatically —
  see `.lore/test-commands.yml` for how this repo exposes descriptors.

- If this round completes what a `specs/<name>/spec.md` describes, update
  that spec's `| Status |` header row in the same branch (Draft ->
  Implemented/Shipped) so the status never lags the code.

BEFORE YOU EDIT A SYMBOL, ask the graph which tests already cover it:
`lore-query-trace` with `tests_covering` set to the file you are about to
change, and `ranges` as `start-end` when you know the span. The rows name
test FILES, because coverage is recorded per file, and they describe the
repository as main last projected it.

Main is the right coordinate for this question: a REGRESSION is by
definition a test that existed before your branch. That list is what tells
a red test apart from one. When CI's verdict on your last push names a
red test you did not write and the acceptance list does not hold, it is
a regression YOU caused — stop, fix the
code, and never "fix" the test. Say in your final message how many red
tests were yours and how many were regressions.

RULES:
- Do not fix unrelated smells you notice. Name them in your final message;
  act on none of them.
- Keep `.lore/dod.md` current: TICK the box of the facet you closed
  (`- [ ]` becomes `- [x]`) and append any new facet you discovered as an
  unchecked one. It is a live checklist, not an append-only log, and the
  next round reads it to see where the ticket actually stands.
- Commit when the test YOU wrote is green. Acceptance tests may still be
  red — that is the ordinary state mid-ticket, and the next round takes
  the next facet.
- If `/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/bbac9678eaf9/workspace/round-brief.md` exists, read it before `.lore/dod.md`. Its
  `The previous round reported` section is where the last round stopped.
  Its `CI reported failures` section is the verdict
  on the previous push, and it outranks `.lore/dod.md`: a red build means
  the ticket is NOT done, however many facets are ticked. Every finding
  it lists — each `path:line message` — is work this round owes before
  anything else. Fix ALL of them in this visit, format, push; there is no
  local re-run here that would show you the rest, and each finding you
  leave costs the ticket a pod and a CI cycle. Run 2a291314 spent two
  rounds reading a ticked dod.md and reporting "nothing left" under a
  verdict naming three lines; the guard sent it to repair each time. Do
  not re-run the whole build to find the failures; the section names them.

DELIVERY, NON-NEGOTIABLE — the next step runs in a DIFFERENT container:
- Before you commit, run the repository's FORMATTER over the files you
  changed (`npx prettier --write <files>`, `gofmt -w <files>`, whichever
  this repo uses) and nothing else from CI's checklist. Do NOT run the
  linter in this pod: CI runs it on every push, and here it does not
  fit — in this repository a two-file `eslint` peaks near 800 MB against
  a 1Gi pod, and runs 112256d9 and 62c1ca5e were OOM-killed on exactly
  that. A lint finding comes back as a red build naming the file and
  line, which the next round fixes with an editor.
- Do NOT typecheck here either. A green test is not a compiled build —
  vitest transpiles each file without checking types — but CI's build
  step is what proves it, and in this repository `tsc --noEmit` on
  `libs/shared` peaks near 950 MB against the 1Gi pod: run 2a291314's
  dod pod was OOM-killed on it. A type error comes back as a red build
  whose failed step and log tail name the file and line; the next
  round fixes it there. Read your imports and signatures twice instead.
- NEVER run a workspace build in this pod (`npm run build`, `tsc -b`, a
  `tsc` without `--noEmit`): tests resolve every workspace package from
  SOURCE, so nothing needs building for a test to see your change, and
  the build is the 950 MB step that OOM-killed run abac6ee9 while it
  rebuilt libs/shared for a test that never needed it.
- When the work is done, `git -C /var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/bbac9678eaf9/workspace/target add` what you changed and commit it with a
  short, factual message. Then `git -C /var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/bbac9678eaf9/workspace/target push origin HEAD`. The clone carries
  its own credentials, so a plain push authenticates; you need no token
  and must never look for one.
- Then bring the branch up to date with its base — `git fetch origin main`
  and merge `origin/main` in — and push again if that produced anything.
  A branch that cannot merge cleanly gets NO CI AT ALL: GitHub runs no
  workflow on a conflicted pull request, so the ticket parks on a build
  that will never start. Resolve any conflict now, favouring `origin/main`
  for anything this ticket did not write, and never by discarding your own
  work. This is why a nine-day-old branch stalled: 186 commits of drift,
  no checks, and a wait with nothing to wait for.
- Confirm it landed: `git status` must report the branch is not ahead of
  its upstream. An unpushed commit lives only in this container and
  dies with it — do NOT report success for one.
- If you genuinely changed nothing, say why — and read the result lines
  below before you choose one: "nothing left to write" and "I am stuck"
  are different endings here, and only the second is a failure.
- Do not open a pull request: you have no `gh` and no GitHub token. Lore
  opens the PR from the branch you push.

THE LAST LINE YOU PRINT is how the round ends. Print exactly one, on its
own line, as the final thing in your message. You are NOT deciding whether
the ticket is done — the build decides that, after your push. You are
reporting whether this round delivered anything.
- You committed and pushed a round:
  LORE_NODE_RESULT: {"outcome":"success","extras":{"tdd_done":"<the facet you closed>","tdd_next":"<the facet the next round takes, or 'acceptance green'>"}}
  This is the ordinary outcome, whether or not acceptance tests remain
  red. CI reads the branch next and sends you back if there is more.
- You wrote nothing because there was nothing left to write — every facet
  in `.lore/dod.md` is closed, its acceptance tests pass, AND no
  `CI reported failures` section is in the round brief (a red verdict IS something
  left to write; fix its findings and report the line above instead):
  LORE_NODE_RESULT: {"outcome":"success","extras":{"tdd_next":"acceptance green"}}
  SUCCESS, not failure. The branch is already pushed; the build judges it
  next, and a green one sends the ticket to review. Reporting failure for
  a round that found the work already done ENDS THE TICKET and strands its
  work on an open branch — which is exactly how run ae788c93 died with the
  implementation complete and all four facets checked off.
- You cannot name a next facet, or the bar will not go green: say exactly
  what blocks you, then:
  LORE_NODE_RESULT: {"outcome":"failed","extras":{"tdd_blocked":"<one line: what blocks you>"}}
  "This is hard" is not stuck; "there is no facet I can express as a test"
  is. Report failure when you are STUCK, never when you are FINISHED.

Author: vvondruska <2923801+vvondruska@users.noreply.github.com>
Date:   Tue Oct 6 13:42:56 2026 +0200

    feat(session): list a user's conversations from the store (#146)
    
    * feat(session): list a user's conversations from the store
    
    Resume rejoins one conversation - the id a client names, or the user's
    latest - and no store member could say which conversations exist, so a
    consumer wanting a conversation list had to query the collection behind
    the engine's back.
    
    Adds the optional `SessionStore.listFor(userId, options?)`, answering
    `SessionSummary` rows (sessionId, createdAt, updatedAt, entryCount) most
    recent activity first, with `limit` (50 default, 200 cap) and `before`
    paging. A summary carries neither entries nor credentials.
    
    InMemorySessionStore reads the activity `latestFor` already computes, so
    a list's first row is always the session a resume would rejoin. Mongo
    filters on the user in the query, sorts on the index `latestFor` needs
    and projects the entries away; `save` now writes an `entryCount` field
    so a list counts a conversation without reading one.
    
    Refs #143
    Relates to re-cinq/Otto#313
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    
    * fix(session): page a conversation list on a total order
    
    Paging on `updatedAt` alone dropped a conversation whenever two of a
    user's shared an activity time and the page boundary fell between them:
    three sessions created in the same millisecond listed the first page and
    then answered nothing, so two conversations were unreachable.
    
    `SessionListOptions.before` is now a `SessionCursor` of `updatedAt` and
    `sessionId` - the last summary the caller saw satisfies it - and both
    stores order on that pair, so a tie cannot straddle a boundary. Mongo
    sorts `{updatedAt: -1, _id: -1}` and filters the tie with `$or`.
    
    A limit of 0 now answers nothing rather than one row. Mongo is never
    asked for it: the driver reads `limit: 0` as no limit at all and would
    have answered with every conversation the filter matched. A limit that
    is not a usable number reads as none given.
    
    In-memory `listFor` and `latestFor` now break a tie differently - id
    against creation order - which the spec and docs state.
    
    Refs #143
    
    * fix(session): make a conversation cursor and its index hold up
    
    An independent review found three defects and an undeclared break.
    
    A cursor whose updatedAt had been through JSON - which is how any real
    client pages - threw a TypeError in memory and silently matched nothing
    on mongo, so a client read a truncated history as the end of it.
    SessionCursor.updatedAt now takes a Date, an ISO string or an epoch
    number, and one carrying no usable moment is refused by name rather than
    read as no cursor at all.
    
    listFor sorts on two keys, which the documented {userId, updatedAt}
    index cannot satisfy: mongo answered a 50-row page by sorting all 300
    of a user's conversations, so paging a long history was quadratic and a
    large one could exceed the 100MB sort limit outright. The index to
    create is now three keys, and a test pins that the two-key form sorts
    where the three-key form does not.
    
    MongoSessionStore.latestFor had no tie-break, so on equal updatedAt it
    answered the opposite end of the tie from listFor while the spec claimed
    they agreed. It now breaks the tie by _id.
    
    CollectionLike is exported, so the required `find` this branch added
    broke any consumer's hand-written adapter. It is optional now, listFor
    refuses a collection without it rather than reporting an empty history,
    and CursorLike, FindManyOptions and FindOneOptions are exported for
    anyone implementing one.
    
    Refs #143
    
    * test(session): pin that both stores answer one conversation list
    
    Closes the review's remaining gaps. A new suite drives the in-memory and
    mongo stores through the same conversations and asserts they answer one
    order - activity apart and tied - and page identically through the
    documented `{limit, before: rows.at(-1)}` call, which no test exercised
    with a limit above one. Writing it caught a bug in itself first: both
    scenarios shared one collection, so the second run's upserts overwrote
    the first's.
    
    The summary-shape test asserted undefined on an object literal it had
    built, which proved nothing. It now reads a real summary out of a store
    created with credentials and pins its exact key set, so a later change
    that let an entry or a header into the row fails here.
    
    A negative limit no longer answers an empty list. It reads as no limit
    given, like a non-finite one, since an empty history for a typo is the
    worse reading; only an explicit 0 answers nothing.
    
    Also: the spec status takes the canonical `Shipped`, and the changelog
    no longer implies the engine serves the list - the store answers it and
    the consumer still writes the route.
    
    Refs #143
    
    * docs(session): say how to tell a conversation list has more pages
    
    listFor answers an array and no hasMore, which left a consumer to invent
    the pattern or, worse, to reach for count(). The listing section now
    documents the short-page and over-fetch readings, including that the 200
    cap tops the over-fetch out at a page of 199.
    
    The count() note said what it counts but never whose: every user's, not
    one user's, so putting it in front of a user both misreports their
    history and discloses the size of everyone else's. A per-user count is
    re-cinq/HALEngine#147.
    
    Refs #143
    
    * docs(session): measure the list query as the store actually issues it
    
    The claim that the three-key index made a page a covered query came from
    a probe projecting only _id. The store projects createdAt and entryCount
    too, neither of which is in the index, so mongo still fetches every row
    it answers with: a 50-row page examines 50, not none. The two-key figure
    stands - it examines all 300.
    
    The point survives the correction and is now stated as what it is: with
    the index the work is the page, without it the work is the history.
    
    The index test now issues the store's own projection and asserts both
    examined counts beside the sort distinction, so the figures in the docs
    cannot drift from what mongo does again.
    
    Refs #143
    
    ---------
    
    Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

     },

 }
+
+function validateListSessionsMessage(message: Record<string, unknown>): ValidationResult {
+  if (message.limit !== undefined && !isNonNegativeInteger(message.limit)) {
+    return {valid: false, error: 'list_sessions limit must be a non-negative integer'};
+  }
+
+  const frame: ListSessionsMessage =
+    message.limit === undefined ? {type: 'list_sessions'} : {type: 'list_sessions', limit: message.limit};
+  if (message.before === undefined) return {valid: true, data: frame};
+
+  const cursor = parseBeforeCursor(message.before);
+  if (cursor === null) {
+    return {valid: false, error: 'list_sessions before must have a valid sessionId and updatedAt'};
+  }
+
+  return {valid: true, data: {...frame, before: cursor}};
+}
+
+function isNonNegativeInteger(limit: unknown): limit is number {
+  return typeof limit === 'number' && Number.isInteger(limit) && limit >= 0;
+}
+
+function parseBeforeCursor(rawCursor: unknown): {updatedAt: string | number; sessionId: string} | null {
+  if (!isPlainObject(rawCursor)) return null;
+  if (!isValidSessionId(rawCursor.sessionId)) return null;
+  if (!isValidUpdatedAt(rawCursor.updatedAt)) return null;
+  return {updatedAt: rawCursor.updatedAt, sessionId: rawCursor.sessionId};
+}
+
+function isPlainObject(candidate: unknown): candidate is Record<string, unknown> {
+  return typeof candidate === 'object' && candidate !== null && !Array.isArray(candidate);
+}
+
+function isValidSessionId(sessionId: unknown): sessionId is string {
+  return typeof sessionId === 'string' && sessionId.length >= 1 && sessionId.length <= MAX_SESSION_ID_LENGTH;
+}
+
+function isValidUpdatedAt(updatedAt: unknown): updatedAt is string | number {
+  if (typeof updatedAt === 'number') return Number.isFinite(new Date(updatedAt).getTime());
+  if (typeof updatedAt === 'string') {
+    const trimmed = updatedAt.trim();
+    return trimmed.length > 0 && Number.isFinite(new Date(updatedAt).getTime());
+  }
+  return false;
+}

parameters.instruction: Add spec citations in specs/hal-engine-conversation-list/spec.md pointing to the new unit test in src/transport/ws/listSessions.test.ts#L40.
parameters.new_string:
## Over the WebSocket protocol

- `ListSessionsMessage`, `SessionSummaryFrame` and `SessionListMessage` sit in `IncomingMessage` and `OutgoingMessage` and are exported from the package root ([validated by: exports ListSessionsMessage, SessionSummaryFrame and SessionListMessage in the wire unions](../../src/index.test.ts#L19)).
- A client sends `{type: 'list_sessions', limit?, before?}` and receives `{type: 'session_list', sessions}` for the socket's authenticated user, with `createdAt` and `updatedAt` serialised as ISO-8601 strings and any client-supplied `userId` ignored ([validated by: answers list_sessions for the authenticated user with ISO dates, forwarding limit and before while ignoring any client userId](../../src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts#L87), [validated by: answers session_list with ISO dates for session.userId, empty when listFor is absent, and SERVER_ERROR on ws log when listFor fails](../../src/transport/ws/listSessions.test.ts#L40)).
- A store without `listFor` answers `{type: 'session_list', sessions: []}`, and a throwing `listFor` logs an error on the `ws` category and answers `{type: 'error', code: 'SERVER_ERROR'}` ([validated by: answers an empty session_list when the store has no listFor, and SERVER_ERROR with a ws error log when listFor throws](../../src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts#L129), [validated by: answers session_list with ISO dates for session.userId, empty when listFor is absent, and SERVER_ERROR on ws log when listFor fails](../../src/transport/ws/listSessions.test.ts#L40)).
- The validator accepts an optional non-negative integer `limit` and an optional `before` cursor whose `sessionId` is 1–128 characters and whose `updatedAt` parses as a valid timestamp, rejecting any other `list_sessions` payload with `INVALID_MESSAGE` without calling `listFor` ([validated by: accepts a bare list_sessions frame and rejects a malformed limit or before with INVALID_MESSAGE without calling listFor](../../src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts#L161), [validated by: accepts list_sessions with optional limit and before cursor while stripping unknown fields](../../src/transport/ws/validation.test.ts#L24), [validated by: rejects list_sessions when limit is not a non-negative integer or before lacks a valid cursor](../../src/transport/ws/validation.test.ts#L55)).
